title: Choose the visual world for dfCTF
question: The roll assigned Campus Line: the seven categories drawn as a campus transit map. Keep it, take the pick or the category standard, or re-roll.

options.label: Campus Line
options.lineage: Campus wayfinding signage and transit line diagrams
options.thesis: Every category is a line and every case is a station; your progress is a map you ride.
options.viewport: A navy enamel rail with white sign type; the overview leads with the seven-line campus map, stations filled when solved, beside the next case to open.
options.risk: If the map turns into decoration rather than the actual way to navigate and read progress, it becomes a transit costume.

raised.raise: Every case carries a line-and-station code (F3, W1), the same on the map, the library row, and the case header.
Color has one job: a hue means a category line and nothing else; red is reserved for a wrong flag.
Rank comes from weight, case, and reversal onto sign plates, not from ever-larger type; three sizes run the app.
No button chrome: flat enamel plates, no shadows, no gradients.
The map and the library are one space: hovering a station lights its row, and filtering the library dims the other lines.
Exact numbers everywhere: full SHA-256, tabular figures, real minutes and XP.

options.label: Evidence Locker
options.thesis: Every case is a sealed evidence bag; solving it signs the custody log.
options.viewport: Library as a rack of sealed bags with typed case numbers; the open case is a custody form with the flag field as the final signature box.
options.risk: Detective-board and evidence-tape looks are where many forensics and CTF sites land; it can read as a costume and as warm tan.

options.label: Factory Catalog
options.thesis: Every case as a numbered catalog entry on matte black.
options.viewport: A fac-numbered index with one pulse plot owning the field.
options.risk: Color codes in place of words hide the category from a beginner.
options.case: Loses both: students do not know the reference, and coded labels cost clarity.
options.kept: Every case carries a fixed code used everywhere.

options.label: Lexicon Plate
options.thesis: Cases as dictionary entries, color quarantined in bordered plates.
options.viewport: Guide words at the head, entries ranked by apparatus.
options.risk: Reads like a reading app, not a practice tool.
options.case: Loses both: no audience pull, and the dashboard and filters fight the page form.

options.label: Timetable Rack
options.lineage: Pocket airline timetables on a light table
options.thesis: One type size; rank carried by weight, case, and reversal.
options.viewport: A raked rack of slides travelling laterally.
options.risk: Raked containers and lateral travel slow a working screen.
options.case: Loses both: the rake hurts scanning, and the reference is foreign to students.
options.kept: Rank by weight and reversal, not size.

options.label: Metro Tiles
options.thesis: Flat tiles and giant lowercase; type is the interface.
options.viewport: A panorama of category tiles with cropped headlines.
options.risk: Reads as a 2012 phone OS; cropped headings hurt clarity.
options.case: Loses both: dated association and weaker wayfinding than the line map.
options.kept: No button chrome; color fields carry state.

options.label: Convention Catalog
options.thesis: A packed grid of stamp-size cells keyed to a hall map.
options.viewport: Hundreds of thumbnail cells with table codes.
options.risk: Cases have no thumbnails; the grid would be empty boxes.
options.case: Loses both: niche audience, and seven cases cannot fill the form.
options.kept: Map and list are one space.

options.label: Datamatics
options.thesis: Pure black-and-white data fields, barcodes, and sine lattices.
options.viewport: A barcode field with dense numeric margins.
options.risk: Strobing and no color fail the calm, beginner-friendly brief.
options.case: Loses both: hostile to beginners and to category reading.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The CTF platform look, played straight and at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Dark sidebar, a grid of category cards with points, and a progress ring.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other CTF platform by design.
